105607227.title: File:Aerial Photo of Monte Rosa Massif - Wallis - Switzerland (cropped).jpg

ImageDescription.value:
Aerial Photo taken from great height of Monte Rosa Massif in canton Valais (Wallis) of Switzerland. To the left of the Monte Rosa massif is the Gornergletscher (Gorner glacier), to the right the Grenzgletscher (border glacier), both flowing in the direction of the lower border of the picture. The distance between the left and right image borders is about 3.5 to 4 km in reality, so that the area depicted by the image is between about 12 and 16 km2. Note: The highest peaks of the Monte Rosa massif, namely the Dufourspitze (Dufour peak) and the Nordend, are not depicted, they are lying outside of the depicted area and would be some cm upside from the upper border of the image.

ImageDescription.value: Aerial view of the city of Zurich from Lake Zurich. Zurich was the location of the 1913 World's Sunday School Convention attended by the Arrases. Note on slide reads "Zurich and the lake." Edmund F. Arras (7/7/1875-10/19/1951), a prominent Columbus businessman and entrepreneur, founded one of Columbus, Ohio’s first property rental agencies in 1892. Trained as a lawyer, he graduated from OSU law school in 1896 and went on to hold positions in numerous civic groups around the city. He was particularly active within Kiwanis International and was involved with several local religious organizations. In 1913, he and his wife Elizabeth traveled to the World Sunday School Association Convention in Zurich, Switzerland. They continued on to travel extensively throughout Europe documenting their journey through photographs. Due to the timing of their trip, these photos comprise a valuable collection of images of European cities later devastated by war. The Arras family’s lantern slides and negatives include images from their 1913 travels through US east coast cities, Atlantic islands of the Azores, Madeira, Gibraltar and the countries of Algeria, Italy, Switzerland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, England, and Ireland. Also included are images from their 1920 train journey from Chicago to the western US for the Kiwanis Convention in Portland. These photographs include images of Chicago, Denver and western National Parks.
